title: Manufacturing Quality Trainee: Protect Lot Traceability
prompt: You are a quality trainee at fictional Rivet Works. A trolley contains 24 finished components. Its traveler says lot L62; the outer tag says L26. A colleague says the numbers were probably transposed and asks you to sign the dispatch check. Exercise policy says mismatched lot identifiers go to the designated quality-hold area, cannot be relabeled by a trainee, and require the quality lead's release before dispatch. Explain your response and handoff. No machine operation or physical product safety judgment is required.
blurb: Hold an uncertain lot identity and preserve evidence instead of turning a plausible guess into a dispatch record.

rubric.label: Distinguish plausible explanation from verification
rubric.description: Recognizes that the transpose explanation is unverified.

anchors.0: Signs the check because L62 and L26 look like a typing error.
anchors.2: Identifies the mismatch and declines to sign it as verified.
anchors.4: Records both identifiers and the count of 24 without choosing one, preserves the traveler and tag, and states that origin remains unverified.

rubric.label: Apply the supplied hold boundary
rubric.description: Keeps dispatch and relabeling within the authorized process.

anchors.0: Relabels or allows dispatch before quality release.
anchors.2: Places the trolley on quality hold and contacts the lead.
anchors.4: Uses the designated hold process, marks the dispatch status pending without altering source labels, and communicates the restriction to the dispatch colleague.

rubric.label: Make the quality investigation actionable
rubric.description: Provides context and a clear release owner.

anchors.0: Leaves the trolley without telling the lead or treats a reply as release.
anchors.2: Gives the lead the mismatched IDs and quantity.
anchors.4: Adds location and the last known handoff evidence, asks the lead to confirm ownership, and requires explicit release evidence before the dispatch check can be completed.

reference.scenario: You are a quality trainee at fictional Rivet Works. A trolley contains 24 finished components. Its traveler says lot L62; the outer tag says L26. A colleague says the numbers were probably transposed and asks you to sign the dispatch check. Exercise policy says mismatched lot identifiers go to the designated quality-hold area, cannot be relabeled by a trainee, and require the quality lead's release before dispatch. Explain your response and handoff. No machine operation or physical product safety judgment is required.

facts.value: The traveler has the prior station's initials and a time of 10:20; the trolley is in bay 4. No verified link to either lot is otherwise supplied.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks what traceability evidence exists

facts.value: The designated quality-hold area has space. The quality lead is reachable now and can investigate the prior station record.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about containment or investigation resources

model_points: A transpose is one possible explanation, not verified identity. Preserve both labels and the count rather than making the evidence agree artificially.
Use the supplied quality-hold process and no trainee relabeling. This exercise does not establish whether the components themselves are defective.
Give the quality lead useful traceability facts and an explicit dispatch boundary; only the authorized release permits completion of the check.

probes.trigger: candidate says the batch is defective rather than unidentified
probes.question: What does the label mismatch actually establish about these components?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes photographing the records before holding the trolley
probes.question: What status and authorized owner still prevent dispatch while the evidence is reviewed?

probes.trigger: candidate initially corrects one label then realizes this was unsupported
probes.question: How would you preserve the original discrepancy and disclose the change to the quality lead?

fair_alternatives: A written hold note or a direct handoff with a traceable record is acceptable.
Photographs or copied labels may support evidence if the fictional site permits them; they do not replace the hold and release process.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess traceability, evidence preservation, and the supplied quality-hold boundary. Do not request machinery procedures, real quality regulations, or product-safety certification. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess traceability, evidence preservation, and the supplied quality-hold boundary. Do not request machinery procedures, real quality regulations, or product-safety certification. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Write a lot-hold record
learning_drills.prompt: Write a concise hold record with both IDs, quantity, location, evidence, and the requested release owner. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Do not choose an ID by appearance
Do not claim product defect from identity uncertainty
